newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks end strongly, led by conglomerates.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks end strongly, led by conglomerates.

text.p: Shares of Nigeria's largest conglomerates finished strongly on Friday, ending another bullish week of trading at the stock exchange, dealers said.
The all-share index rose to 8729.52 from Thursday's 8699.71, and compared with the week's opening level of 8667.61 on Monday.
"There is nothing to suggest that the current boom in share trading is fading," said one trader.
West African Portland Cement Company topped gainers, rising 80 kobo to close at 65.00 naira.
United African Company closed at 19.00 naira, up by 55 kobo while Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company gained 50 kobo to 54.50 naira.
Union Dicon Salt and Cadbury gained 20 kobo each to finish, respectively, at 50.60 naira and 39.80 naira. Lever Brothers ended 10 kobo higher at 28.60 naira.
John Holt and Delta Glass both rose 10 kobo apiece to 9.90 naira and 9.70 naira, respectively.
Banking shares performed strongly with United Bank for Africa at 14.80 naira, 20 kobo firmer while NAL Merchant Bank rose 12 kobo to close at 7.82 naira.
Oil marketer Agip led the losers, slumping 25 kobo to 27.00 naira while Van Leer Containers finished at 10.40 naira, 20 kobo down.
Ashaka Cement, Afprint and stationery makers Thomas Wyatt were each 10 kobo down to 14.20 naira, 1.94 naira and 4.50 naira, respectively.
